title: How Pieter Levels runs ~$3M/yr of automated indie sites solo with open revenue stats
summary: Levels explains how he runs Nomad List, Remote OK and other sites with one part-time contractor team, a deliberately simple PHP/jQuery stack, near-total automation and public revenue stats. He argues a $20k/month app is already a ~$1M asset, explains why he won't sell or raise VC, and credits radical transparency as a recurring marketing machine.

principles.text: Pick whatever stack gives the fastest feedback loop; it matters more than the tech.
principles.quote: it doesn't matter what you use, but as long as you use something that's really fast um, feedback loop and iterative loop where you can really quickly develop.

principles.text: Fast shipping makes customers happy because they see their feedback become product.
principles.quote: if you want happy customers, that's how you get it. You make something for them. They're like, "Oh my god, I influenced this product."

principles.text: A $20k/month app is already roughly a $1M asset, a far more reachable goal than a unicorn.
principles.quote: it's reachable, especially if you think about high automation, very high margins.

principles.text: Keep margins high with automation and part-time contractors instead of hiring a big team.
principles.quote: you work with part-time contracts like I do and you keep your margins very, very high because then you can sell for five x

principles.text: Even high-ticket sales can be fully automated via a self-serve Stripe checkout with a bundle slider.
principles.quote: I sell job post bundles for like 50k via stripe.

principles.text: Publishing open numbers and ups and downs is a recurring marketing machine that fuels audience and growth.
principles.quote: it's this recurring marketing machine that I think it's a big part of why my business is work became successful and why I got a lot of audience on Twitter
